public_evidence_label: Anthropic (Ireland) invoice and receipt: one-time API credit purchase, reverse charge, 0% VAT
notes: A manual purchase, paid by card at 23:16 UTC after a failed attempt at 23:13 UTC. The receipt date is Sep 19; in Warsaw it was Sep 20, 01:16. Both dates give the same preceding NBP business day (Sep 18). Sentinel classification resumed at 23:19:57 UTC. It is the first invoice from the new Irish billing entity. The deleted-mail inventory had wrongly tagged this receipt as a Max subscription; the portal invoice shows an API credit purchase. Consumed to Oct 14: Sentinel 0.8846 (Sep 19-20), msigalert 0.3591 (Sep 20 to Oct 13). That leaves 18.756 unconsumed, against the Console's 18.77. The FIFO simulation also leaves $0.0034 of Sentinel's Sep 17 usage beyond the simulated balance. If Anthropic let the balance dip that far below zero, this grant settled it and Sentinel's share would be 0.888 (0.0444). The Console balance sits above the simulation, not below it, so this is treated as rounding and not booked. FIFO share as of Oct 14 is 4.4%. Trigger-based attribution would put the whole $20 on Sentinel; that is an owner decision (open question).

public_evidence_label: OpenRouter credit purchase: Stripe receipt via the provider portal, invoice showing 23% PL VAT, and a deleted-mail receipt snippet
notes: Paid on 2026-09-23 at 20:09:15 UTC. $40.00 of credits cost $51.91, which is $42.20 net (credits plus the 5.5% fee) plus $9.71 VAT; cash per credit is 1.29775. The owner bought it during the Sentinel eval round, after choosing an eval budget of about $35. The prompt for it was the assistant's line 'The eval key has $4.17 left, so any option needs a top-up there'. That $4.17 was the remainder of the key's own $5 spending LIMIT, not the account balance; the account then held about $23.39. Raising the key limit was needed in any case. A top-up was consistent with the chosen $35 budget, which was larger than $23.39, but in the end Sentinel spent only $2.33 after this purchase, which the old balance covered. By FIFO none of this lot has been consumed: all usage to 2026-10-14 ($4.2155) fits inside the first $25 lot. Sentinel's share is therefore 0, and the whole $40 sits in the unspent $60.78 balance. The bundle's email verifier attributed this purchase to Sentinel by purchase intent; the agreed FIFO convention supersedes that, and the alternative is kept as an open question.
